Recent building maintenance included a new lift, and the parish is now focused on modernising its school facilities.

n: Meerut St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church

n: New Delhi-Hauz Khas St. Mary's Malankara Orthodox Cathedral

Sixteen prayer groups meet each month across Delhi, alongside a 150-student Sunday School, MGOCSM, the Youth Movement, Martha Mariam Samajam, AMOSS, and a dedicated Diaspora ministry. The Cathedral's reach extends through St. George Chapel in Aya Nagar, St. Paul's Schools in Hauz Khas (2,200+ students) and Aya Nagar (1,650 students), and St. Mary's Medical Centre, a 24-hour facility serving more than 16,000 patients a year as an approved DOTS tuberculosis centre.

n: Noida St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church

n: Rohini St. Basil Malankara Orthodox Church

The parish also runs AANCHAL, a centre for differently abled children that marked its tenth anniversary this year, and is seeking a vehicle to support the centre's outreach.

n: Sarita Vihar St. Thomas Malankara Orthodox Church

A 32-student Sunday School, MGOCSM, Martha Mariam Samajam, the Youth Movement, and Acolytes support parish life, alongside St. Thomas Pre-School. The community runs medical camps and distributes food and clothing to the underprivileged while working toward a sustainable income plan for daily operations.

n: Sharjah St. Gregorios Indian Orthodox Church
ds:
2,300 families (2022) - The parish Sunday School has 1,600 students. Moved to Madras Diocese from Delhi Diocese in August of 2026 in order to financially support the diocese.

Around 3500 to 4000 people attend the Holy Qurbana. Holy Qurbana is celebrated on all Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. n: Tughlaqabad St. Joseph Malankara Orthodox Church
ds: 45 families (2026) - St. Joseph's Orthodox Church, Tughlakabad, serves South Delhi with about 110 worshippers at Sunday Holy Qurbana. A 20-child Sunday School, MGOCSM, the Youth Movement, Martha Mariam Samajam, and Acolytes are active alongside St. Joseph Pre School. The foundation stone for a new church building was laid on 9 October 2025, and the parish supports educational assistance through its Vidhya Project.

By 1985, the Diocesan headquarters moved to its own building, the Delhi Orthodox Centre in Tughlaqabad in South Delhi. An architecturally distinctive three-storey building, the centre was dedicated by Catholicos Baselios Mar Thoma Mathews I and inaugurated by the Vice-President of India, R Venkataraman, in November 1984. With the St. Thomas Chapel in the middle, the centre is the residence of the Metropolitan and houses, besides the secretariat of the Diocesan Council, a library, a publication unit, the People's Education Society, Sophia Society, Sarva Dharma Nilaya, Dhyan Mandir and Niti Santi Kendra, engaged in a variety of complementary activities. In 1991, the Diocese was strengthened by the arrival of Job Mar Philoxenos as the Assistant Metropolitan.

n: Kuala Lumpur St. Mary's Indian Orthodox Cathedral (Brickfields)
ds:
200 families (2018) - There are 630 Malankara Orthodox laity in Malaysia and 2 priests serving across 6 congregations under this parish.

The first parish that the Malankara Orthodox Church had outside India was Malaya-Singapore. These two places, under British colonial rule, had many tea, coffee and rubber estates. Most
of the labourers in those estates were Tamils and Chinese. A large number of Christians from Kerala were also employed as the overseers and office staff. Most of these people were from Central Travancore and majority of them were Marthomites (largest minority was Orthodox). They had six or seven churches and one school there. The Orthodox had one church each in Malaya and Singapore. There was a joint
council for these two churches which worked hard to see that the vicars could easily carry out their responsibilities.

Originally the priest would come via ship from Madras to Singapore to Penang to Kuala Lumpur serving the congregations in the three cities.

Parish of H. G. Abraham Mar Epiphanios Metropolitan, first Malankara Orthodox bishop born outside India.

ds: The orthodox church activities for lonavla was started in the year 1958 by late mr t.V koruthu. He was elected as a member of the managing committee of kirkee/pune orthodox syrian church in 1960. Holy qurbana was celebrated at lonavla on holidays, 26th january & 15th august and also on the 5th sunday of the month . The vicar of kirkee/pune used to come to lonavla for conducting the service. Sunday prayer meetings started on a regular basis from the year 1971. Since 1958 till today we conduct the holy qurbana at “all saints church” (csi) barabunglow lonavala on rent. Under the guidance of rev fr p.V kuriakose we formed mgm prayer group at lonavla in the year 1977. A plot of land about 4500 sq ft was purchased for building a church on 06/12/1987 in the joint names of four members, t.V kunjumen,alexander koruthu,k.J.George and koshy varghese . Foundation stone for building a small church was laid by late lamented his grace phillipose mar theophilus on 26.04.1990. There were only fifteen members at that time and due to insufficient funds the project could not be completed. The land was transferred in the name of metropolitan of bombay, his grace geevarghese mar coorilos on 07.04.2000. Since 1988 holy qurbana is offered once in a month at lonavala. Presently rev fr john mathai is our vicar. The lonavala parshiners attend the services like christmas,holy week, easter, pentecost and other feast days in dehuroad/ chinchwad/kirkee/pune church. Even though lonavla being such a small congregation of only nine family members, his grace geevarghese mar coorilos has celebrated the holy qurbana several times at lonavala, we are very thankful to our beloved thirumeni.

ds: ST MARY’S ORTHODOX SYRIAN CHURCH, NERUL Since 1985, Orthodox believers of Nerul node were attending the Holy Mass at St. Thomas Aramana Chruch, Vashi and prayer meetings had been going on at member’s residences on Sundays at Nerul, led by Rev Fr Thomas Varghese and Rev Fr T U Thomas. With the expansion of the township and a surge in Orthodox believers, St Mary’s Congregation came into existence. In 2004 it was declared as a parish. Holy Qurbana were conducted twice a month. Initially it started with 49 members. At present there are 111 members on the roll. From 2004 onwards there are regular services. Rev Fr T E Issac, Rev Fr Joji George, Rev Fr Abraham Joseph, Rev Fr M E Joseph & Rev Fr Thomas Mathai served as vicars. During this period, Sunday services were conducted at different places like CIDCO Community hall, Nerul, Meridian Apartments, Sector 6-Nerul, St Augustine’s High School, Sector11-Nerul, Municipal High School, Sector 4-Nerul and Municipal High School, Sector 20-Nerul. On 16th March 2011, the church members with the combined efforts of Rev Fr M E Joseph and managing committee formed a trust names “St Mary’s Orthodox Trust” and registered with the charity commissioner, Thane. This is in fact a great achievement. Subsequently, in 2012, with the co-operation and effort of members, a 3 BHK flat was purchased at sector 27, Nerul (E). Spiritual organizations like Sunday School, MGOCSM, OCYM, MMVS and Cottage prayer meetings are functioning regularly. Rev Fr K P Varghese is the present Vicar.

Built in colonial architectural style, it served as a major place of worship for the families of British soldiers stationed in the Secunderabad Cantonment. After Independence on March 5, 1948 the Government of India entrusted the church to the United Malayalam Congregation (combined Orthodox, Marthoma and CSI). The Orthodox Parish was established in 1951, with H.G. Mathews Mar Barnabas serving as the parish's first vicar (Fr. K.K. Mathew at the time). 

The old church was demolished and a new church was consecrated in March 2005 when the sacred relics of St. Gregorios of Parumala and St. Dionysius of Vattasseril were installed.

ds: കേളകം സെന്റ്‌ ജോര്‍ജ്ജ് ഓര്‍ത്തഡോക്‍സ്‌ വലിയപള്ളി,പരിശുദ്ധ ഗീവര്‍ഗീസ്‌ സഹദായുടെ നാമത്തില്‍ സ്ഥാപിക്കപ്പെട്ട ഉത്തരമലബാറിലെ ആദ്യദേവാലയം.1955ല്‍ പള്ളി സ്ഥാപിക്കപ്പെട്ടു .1956 september 20 നു ബഹുമാനപ്പെട്ട ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ അച്ചന്‍(വല്യച്ചന്‍) ഇടവകയുടെ വികാരിയായി,50 വര്‍ഷത്തില്‍ അധികം ഇടവകയെ നയിച്ചു.ഇപ്പോള്‍ വികാരിയായി Fr.Samson.M.Simon സേവനം അനുഷ്ടിക്കുന്നു.180 ല്‍ പരം കുടുംബങ്ങള്‍ ഇന്ന് ഇടവകയില്‍ ഉണ്ട്.മലങ്കരസഭയുടെ അഭിമാനമായ ഈ പള്ളി ഉത്തരമലബാറില്‍ ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ സഹദായുടെ നാമത്തില്‍ വിളക്ക്നേര്‍ച്ച ഉള്ള ഏക ദേവാലയമാണ്.എല്ലമാസത്തെയും അവസാനത്തെ വെള്ളിയാഴ്ച വിളക്ക്നേര്‍ച്ച നടക്കുന്നു.മലങ്കര സഭയുടെ എല്ലാ തലത്തിലും ശ്രദ്ധിക്കപ്പെടുന്ന നേട്ടങ്ങളും സേവനങ്ങളും കാഴ്ചവെക്കുന്ന ഇടവകയെ പ.കാതോലിക്കാബാവ 2010ല്‍ വലിയപള്ളിയായി ഉയര്‍ത്തി.ഇടവക അംഗമായ ശ്രി .പൈലി വാത്യട്ടു സഭാ മാനേജിംഗ് കമ്മിറ്റി മെംബര്‍ ആണ്.മലങ്കര സഭയുടെ ബത്തേരി ഭദ്രാസനത്തിലെ പ്രധാന ദേവാലയങ്ങളില്‍ ഒന്നാണ് ഈ പള്ളി.നമ്മെ വിട്ട്പിരിഞ്ഞ ഇടവകയുടെ ശില്പിയും നമ്മുടെ ആത്മീയ ഗുരുവും ആയിരുന്ന വല്യച്ചന്റെ സ്നേഹനിര്‍ഭരമായ ഓര്‍മ്മയില്‍,പ്രാര്‍ത്ഥനയോടെ എല്ലാ ഇടവക അംഗങ്ങളെയും ഈ ഗ്രൂപ്പിലേക്ക് സ്വാഗതം ചെയുന്നു.

On National Highway 66, about 80 kilometres North from the port city of Mangalore in Southern India, is a town called Brahmavar, where a treacherous turn blinded truck and bus drivers from spotting villagers crossing beyond the bend and, over the years, hundreds were crushed into gruesome injuries and often, death.
At the turn of the millennium, in Year 2000, one of them happened to be the kin of Fermin D’Souza, a Brahmavar veteran, whose home was just off that deadly point. Her daughter and grand daughter survived after multiple injuries but she lost one of her family.

Fermin, along with her son Francis, then 55 years old, sought the advice of priests at their St. Mary’s Syrian Orthodox Cathedral and was advised to install a ‘Holy Cross’ at the turn.
Village elders counselled that it would have real results only if speeding drivers noticed divinity beyond the bend, so they would slow down, to look and pay homage. There needed to be a cross erected high, and imposing enough, to be seen above the blind spot.

And so work began – a solid mass concrete cross was ordered with its height above the altar platform standing at 18 feet and spanning 12 feet wide. Weighing close to two tons, it was a civil-engineering challenge for the village devout. The Holy Cross tilted in the mushy soil of South Kanara’s heavy rainfall zone.

A crane had to be pressed into service. After it was installed, the number of accidents around the bend dropped drastically. Over the years, Belief in the Holy Cross of the House of Thikhar grew and hardened inter-state truck drivers stopped to offer homage and drop a few coins in offerings.

It evolved as Francis’ ‘Thikhar’ family installed a clean-water tap for those who stopped by to wash away the heat and humidity of the tropical road and to fill their bottles for their hard journey ahead. Thikhar means ‘gemstones dealer’, a name inherited from Francis’ great grandfather who dealt in semi-precious stones, bartering them for coastal goods such as coir products.
Can’t say if it is just by sheer coincidence, or destiny, that Francis, a Thikhar descendant, one hundred years later also worked with precious stones, in diamonds in Mumbai.

മെത്രാപ്പോലീത്ത നി.വ.ദി. ശ്രീ. വയലിപ്പറമ്പിൽ ഗീവർഗീസ് മോർ ഗ്രീഗോറിയോസ് തിരുമേനിയുടെ കൽപ്പനയാൽ ബഹുമാനപ്പെട്ട പടിഞ്ഞാറേകുടിയിൽ മത്തായി വർക്കി കശീശ 1955 ഫെബ്രുവരി മാസം ആറാം തീയതി പ്രഥമ ബലിയർപ്പിച്ച് ആരംഭിച്ചതാണ് ഈ മാതൃദേവാലയം.

ശാന്തൻപാറ, തൊട്ടിക്കാനം, മുരുക്കുംതൊട്ടി അരിവിളംചാൽ മുട്ടുകാട് എന്നീ പ്രദേശങ്ങളിലായി ഉണ്ടായിരുന്ന 71 കുടുംബങ്ങളാണ് ഈ ദേവാലയത്തിലെ ആദ്യ ഇടവകാംഗങ്ങൾ. പിന്നീട് ഈ ദേവാലയത്തിൽ നിന്നും മുരുക്കും തൊട്ടി സെന്റ് ജോർജ് യാക്കോബായ സുറിയാനി പള്ളി, പഴയ വിടുതി സെന്റ് മേരിസ് യാക്കോബായ സുറിയാനി പള്ളി, മുട്ടുകാട് സെന്റ് തോമസ് യാക്കോബായ സുറിയാനി പള്ളി, സെന്റ് ജോർജ് യാക്കോബായ സുറിയാനി പള്ളി, മാങ്ങാത്തൊട്ടി മോർ ഗ്രിഗോറിയോസ് യാക്കോബായ സുറിയാനി പള്ളി, വട്ടപ്പാറ സെന്റ് മേരിസ് യാക്കോബായ സുറിയാനി പള്ളി, ശാന്തൻപാറ സെന്റ് ജോർജ് യാക്കോബായ സുറിയാനി പള്ളി എന്നിവ പല കാലങ്ങളിൽ ആയി പിരിഞ്ഞു പോയി. ഇപ്പോൾ ഈ ഇടവകയിൽ 500 പരം കുടുംബങ്ങളും 2500 ഓളം ഇടവക അംഗങ്ങളും ഉണ്ട്.

ഈ ഇടവകയുടെ ആദ്യ ഭരണ സമിതി അംഗങ്ങൾ ശ്രീ.പി വി മത്തായി പിള്ള പടിഞ്ഞാറേ കുടിയിൽ ശ്രീ പൈലി പാപ്പച്ചൻ അമ്പഴച്ചാലിൽ,ശ്രീ കെ വി ഫിലിപ്പോസ് കൂരാപ്പിള്ളിൽ, ശ്രീ മത്തായി പൈലി ഇലവുംകുടി വീട്ടിൽ എന്നിവർ ആയിരുന്നു.
ഇപ്പോൾ വികാരി പ്രസിഡന്റായും, സഹവികാരി, തന്നാണ്ട് വാർഷിക പൊതുയോഗത്തിൽ തിരഞ്ഞെടുക്കപ്പെടുന്ന ട്രസ്റ്റിമാർ,ഐടിസി സെക്രട്ടറി,കമ്മിറ്റി അംഗങ്ങൾ ഉൾപ്പെടുന്ന മാനേജിംഗ് കമ്മിറ്റി ഭരണം നടത്തിവരുന്നു.

ഈ പള്ളിയുടെ കീഴിൽ രാജകുമാരി സൗ ത്തിൽ സ്‌തേഫാനോ സ് സഹദായുടെയും ബസേലിയോസ് ബാവയുടെയും സംയുക്ത നാമധേയത്തിൽ ഒരു ചാപ്പലും, പള്ളിയുടെ പടിഞ്ഞാറ് ഭാഗത്തായി കുര്യാക്കോസ് സഹദായുടെയും കിഴക്കുഭാഗത്തായി റോഡിനോട് ചേർന്ന് വിശുദ്ധ ഗീവർഗീസ് സഹദായുടെ കുരിശും രാജകുമാരി നോർത്ത് ടൗണിൽ വിശുദ്ധ ദൈവ മാതാവിന്റെ കുരിശുംതൊട്ടിയും, എം പി.റ്റി.പടിയിൽ വിശുദ്ധ ഗീവർഗീസ് സഹദായുടെ കുരിശും തൊട്ടിയും,രാജകുമാരി സൗത്തിൽ പരിശുദ്ധ പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ കുരിശും തൊട്ടിയും, കുളക്കോഴിച്ചാൽ ഭാഗത്ത് തോമാശ്ലീഹായുടെ കുരിശും തൊട്ടിയും ബി ഡിവിഷൻ ഭാഗത്ത് ദൈവമാതാവിന്റെയും മോർ ബസേലിയോസ് ബാവ യുടെയും നാമത്തിലുള്ള കുരിശും തൊട്ടിയും, ജണ്ടനിരപ്പ് ഭാഗത്ത് ഗീവർഗീസ് സഹദായുടെ നാമത്തിലുള്ള കുരിശും തൊട്ടിയും സ്ഥാപിച്ചിട്ടുള്ളതാകുന്നു.
പള്ളിയുടെ കീഴിൽ 18 കുടുംബയൂണിറ്റുകളും, കുര്യാക്കോസ്‌ സഹദായുടെയും മോർ ബസേലിയോസ്ബാവയുടെയും നാമത്തിൽ രണ്ട് സൺഡേ സ്കൂളുകളും, സെന്റ് ജോൺസ് യൂത്ത് അസോസിയേഷനും, മോർ ബസേലിയോസ് യൂത്ത് അസോസിയേഷനും, പ്രവർത്തിച്ചുവരുന്നു. അതോടൊപ്പം വയലിപ്പറമ്പിൽ ഗീവർഗീസ് മോർ ഗ്രിഗോറിയോസ് തിരുമേനിയുടെ നാമത്തിൽ ഒരു ഐടിഐയും 1978 മുതൽ പ്രവർത്തിച്ചിരുന്നു

115 families (2022) - In 1939, the Reverend Mulavarikkal Paulose Ramban established the Seenai Monastery at Mambra and a Parish church in the name of St. Kuriakose the Martyr. In 1946, he was consecrated as Paulose Mar Severios, the Metropolitan of the Cochin Diocese. In 1950, the Sion Seminary and Chapel were established at Chirangara. Our Parish is under the Diocese of Kochi. Today, 130 devoted members actively participate in various spiritual movements, which include those within this parish, continuing to grow in the divine. H.G. Yuhannon Mar Severios led the diocese from 1966, drawing people with his saintly nature and gentleness. Chapel attendance rose, with regular services on Sundays and special occasions. The parish faced challenges after 1975 due to internal church divisions, including restricted access to sacraments and threats to Sion Seminary. Despite this, the community remained loyal and defended the seminary and its rights. Considering these circumstances, the diocesan Metropolitan's 1979-80 orders formally designated the Seminary Chapel for parish use, appointing Rev. Father Joseph Areeckal as the first vicar, allowing the seminary and parish to function peacefully together.

Priests from this parish: Lt. Fr. Joseph Areeckal, Fr. K.K. Kuriakose, Fr. K.M. Kuriakose, Fr. Eldho T.V., Fr. Poly Varghese T.
Nuns from this parish: Sr. Ruth, Sr. Smooni

8 seminarians (2018) - Sion Seminary, the official headquarters of the Cochin Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, stands as a historic and spiritual center with deep roots in faith and education. It was founded shortly after the establishment of the Cochin Diocese in 1896, with the vision of preparing dedicated servants of God and strengthening the spiritual life of the diocese. The seminary has grown over the years into a nurturing home for theological learning. At its peak, Sion Seminary accommodated over 50 seminarians, shaping many priests who went on to serve parishes across the Church. Today, the seminary continues its mission, with 3-8 seminarians currently undergoing their formation and studies. A notable feature of the seminary is the Chapel, which was built in 1950. The chapel serves as a sacred space for prayer, worship, and spiritual reflection, contributing to the overall mission of the seminary as a place of deepened faith and connection with God. The seminary is administered under the guidance of the Manager, Rev. Fr. Varghese Abraham, who oversees both academic and spiritual activities. The diocese is currently led by H.G. ട്രസ്റ്റിമാർ തΩിലുള്ള ഭിന്നതയിലാരം ഭിച്ച്‌ പ. വട്ടശ്ശേരിൽ മാർ ദീവന്നാസേ്യാസിനെ അബ്‌ദുള്ള ബാവാ മുടക്കിയതോടെ ആവിർഭവിച്ച ഭിന്നത പാലൂർ-ചാട്ടുകുളങ്ങര എന്ന്‌ പുരാതന നാമമുള്ള ആർത്താറ്റ്‌ ഇടവകയിലും പ്രകടമായി. തീരെ ന്യൂനപക്ഷമായതിനാൽ ആ പുരാതനപള്ളിയ്‌ക്കു സമീപം 12 പേരുടെ പേരിൽ അന്തേ്യാഖ്യാസിംഹാസനത്തിന്‌ വേണ്ടി ഒരു സമാന്തര ദേവാലയം പണിയാൻ …ീബാ മാർ ഒസ്‌താത്തിയോസ്‌ നേതൃത്വം നൽകി. 1920 ഒക്‌ടോ. 9 ന്‌ ശിലാസ്ഥാപനം നടത്തി. 1930 മാർച്ച്‌ 19 ന്‌ മാർ ഒസ്‌താത്തിയോസ്‌ കാലം ചെയ്യുന്നതുവരെയും ഇവിടെ താമസിച്ചു ഇവിടെത്തന്നെ കബറടങ്ങി. ഒസ്‌താത്തിയോസിന്‌ ശേഷം മാർ യൂലിയോസ്‌ ചുമതല വഹിച്ചു. 1958-ൽ സഭാഐക്യത്തോടെ പള്ളി കൊച്ചി ഭദ്രാസനത്തിൽ ലയിച്ചു. ഇതിൽ അതൃപ്‌തരായി ഒരു ഗ്രൂപ്പ്‌ വ്യവഹാരം ആരംഭിച്ചത്‌ നിലനില്‌ക്കുന്നു. 1962 മാർച്ച്‌ 17-ന്‌ പൗലൂസ്‌ മാർ സേവേറിയോസ്‌ ഇവിടെ വച്ച്‌ കാലം ചെയ്‌തു 18 ന്‌ ഇവിടെതന്നെ കബറടങ്ങി. ആദ്യകബർ വടക്കുഭാഗത്തും രണ്ടാമത്തെ കബർ തെക്കുഭാഗത്തും പള്ളിയകത്ത്‌ സ്ഥിതിചെയ്യുന്നു.

375 families (2026) - Historically, Kattakampal church was a chapel of Pazhanji church, whose priests occassionally celebrated the Holy Qurbana here. Then Pulikkottil Chiriyaku's wife Kunjitty decided after she had two daughters that if a son is born the son will become the parish priest "Deshathu Pattakkar' of Kattakampal church. When the son passes SSLC, he was sent to MD Seminary for priestly studies at at 19 he was ordained a priest by Pampady Thirumeni at Kumarakom Attamangalam Church on May 7th 1963. Pulikkottil Simon Kathanar was appointed as the Vicar then on June 1st 1953. He was known as "Kattakampalachen" to the people. He then became a teacher and then principal and he used his salary for the church. Now there are 8 cross shrines under this church (3 to the west, 3 to the west and 2 at the church premises). The church also owns land 1/2 acre at south Pattupadam and 1 1/2 acres at Vadakke Pattu field in Punjapadam. The church also has its own shopping complex and building at Erumapetty, a shopping complex at Chirackal and there is an aided LP School under this church. 

Of the 375 families under this church, 250 are Pulikkottil, 50 are Cheruvathoor, 25 are Kattil, Tholath are 35, Vadakke Thalackal are 15, Ayyamkulangara are 4 and Kannanackal are 1.

ds:
Established in 1816 this church is a stronghold of Malankara Orthodox Christians in Puthencruz. One of the main families that supports this parish is the Maliakal Kanneth Family.

The church was established by the members of the Kolenchery Church residing in the area. Initially a cross made of wood was established here when the 'raza' (church procession) during the festival of Kolenchery church reached here, marking the beginning of a church here. This cross was called 'Puthen Kurisu' (New Cross). Later a church was consecrated in the place where the Cross was established and regular services began. Subsequently the village itself came to be known by the same name, 'Puthencruz'.

In late 19th century the sacred relics of Mor Kuriakose Sahdo was interred in this church by St. Gregorios of Parumala, presented to Malankara by Antioch. In 1964, reconstruction of the old church building began under the able leadership of the then church vicar Fr. Thomas Cheruvallil (schismatic) and was consecrated on February 15, 1966 by H.H. Moran Mar Baselios Augen I Catholicos of Malankara.

St. Peter’s & St. Paul’s Orthodox Church, Pathicadu (popularly known as Pathicadu Pally), stands as a venerable and architecturally majestic sanctuary situated approximately one kilometre from Mallappally town in the Pathanamthitta district of Keralam. Falling under the Mallappally ecclesiastical district of the historic Niranam Diocese of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, the parish is deeply rooted in the 19th-century spiritual renaissance of Central Travancore and shares an intimate historical bond with Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios of Parumala.

### History ###
In the early centuries, the Christian faithful of this region depended directly on Niranam St. Mary's Orthodox Syrian Church, traditionally founded by St. Thomas the Apostle, for liturgical worship, the Holy Mysteries, and funeral rites. In an era when overland routes were scarce and arduous, travel relied primarily on boats voyaging along the Manimala River (historically known in Sanskrit literature as the Vishakanah or Vishaghna, celebrated in lore as waters possessing antidotal virtues against venom). Moved by the hardships faced by the faithful, the royal rulers of the Edappally dynasty—renowned for their religious tolerance, generosity, and communal harmony—sanctioned land and consent for a sanctuary at Kallooppara, leading to the foundation of the ancient Kallooppara Church. Later, to relieve the faithful of Mallappally from the arduous journey across the river to Kallooppara, Vengalasserry St. Mary’s Old Syrian Church (Kaattupally) was founded along bank of Manimala River on 13 July 1834 AD [29 Midhunam 1009 ME], eventually becoming one of only five historic sanctuaries in Keralam shared equally between the Orthodox and Mar Thoma church communities following the 19th-century church reformation.

As the Christian population expanded across the countryside, the community recognized the pressing necessity of founding an independent parish at Pathicadu. The land required for the sanctuary was donated by Mr V. Varghese Valakuzhy. With the formal sanction granted by the Edappally royal dynasty and the ecclesiastical consent issued by Malankara Metropolitan Mor Dionysius V (Pulikkottil Joseph Mar Dionysius II), the parish was formally established. On 11 July 1888 AD [29 Midhunam 1063 ME], the cornerstone of the church, dedicated to the Holy Apostles Saint Peter and Saint Paul, was solemnly laid by Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios of Parumala (Parumala Thirumeni), then Metropolitan of the Niranam Diocese. On the very same day, the Saint offered the Holy Qurbana inside a temporary shed. Parumala Thirumeni remained in the settlement for two weeks, personally overseeing the initial construction works before celebrating the parish's first annual patronal feast. For over a century, regular divine worship and the Holy Qurbana continued uninterrupted in the historic church until 13 January 2006 AD [29 Dhanu 1181 ME].
From its formative decades, the parish fostered community upliftment and the Christian upbringing of younger generations. The church instituted the M.D.L.P. School (Mar Dionysius Lower Primary School), Pathicadu, which became an early beacon of elementary education for children from neighboring hamlets. In 1988, the parish observed its Centenary Jubilee marking one hundred years since the laying of the foundation stone by Saint Parumala Thirumeni.

To accommodate the steady growth of the congregation, the general body resolved to reconstruct the church edifice on an ambitious scale. On 15 January 2000, on the auspicious day of the parish feast, the foundation stone for the new church was solemnly laid by HH Moran Mar Baselios Marthoma Mathews II, Catholicos of the East and Malankara Metropolitan, in the presence of HG Dr Geevarghese Mar Osthathios, Metropolitan of the Niranam Diocese, and Rev. n: Vengalassery St. Mary's Orthodox Union Church
ds:
Shared with Marthoma. First church in Mallapally. Known as Kaattupally. The sanction for building this church was given by the then Travancore King Sri. Swathi Thirunal. The foundation stone was laid on 28th Midhunam, Kollavarsham 1009 (Malayalam calendar). The church is situated on the bank of river Manimala and both Marthomite and Orthodox believers worship in the church.

St. Mary’s Old Syrian Church, Vengalasserry, located along the serene banks of the Manimala River in Keezhvaipur, Mallappally, is an ancient landmark of faith and the oldest Syrian church in the region. Situated about 2.5 km from Mallappally town, the sanctuary came to be known locally as 'Kaattupally' due to its remote setting in the dense, secluded woodlands that once covered Vengalasserry Hill. Architecturally, its exterior reflects the rare pre-Portuguese indigenous style, distinguished by an expansive overhang roof extending outward past the front wall. The edifice was traditionally crafted using dressed laterite stone, mud mortar, and indigenous timber, embodying the sustainable, time-honoured craftsmanship of the era. It holds the rare distinction of being one of only five churches in Kerala over which the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church and the Malankara Mar Thoma Syrian Church share equal joint ownership and rights.


History
Historically, the local faithful travelled to the ancient Kallooppara Church (St. Mary’s Orthodox Valiyapally, Kallooppara)—founded nearly 750 years ago—for their liturgical services and religious observances. At the time, with virtually no developed transit routes and the constant peril of wild animal encounters, the journey was arduous and hazardous. These pressing difficulties inspired the believers to establish a church within Mallappally itself, realizing this vision in 1834 AD [1009 ME] and marking the dawn of organized congregational worship in the locality.During the tenure of Cheppad Philipose Mar Dionysius IV as Malankara Metropolitan, a petition was submitted seeking sanction to establish a parish, which His Grace duly approved. Construction initially commenced at the Palliyelkunnel plot near the present-day Taluk Hospital Junction; however, unforeseen local opposition brought the work to a halt. Through the resolute efforts of community elders, an alternative parcel of crown land (Pandaravaka) was secured on the eastern banks of the Manimala River, atop Vengalasserry Hill in Muttathumannu, with the formal royal sanction of the Maharaja of Travancore, H.H. Swathi Thirunal. Authorized by Cheppad Mar Dionysius, Palakkunnathu Abraham Malpan consecrated the holy cross and celebrated the first Holy Qurbana within a temporary chapel on 13 July 1834 AD [29 Midhunam 1009 ME]. Founded on the feast day of the Apostles Saints Peter and Paul, the sanctuary was dedicated in the name of St. Mary. Deacon Palakkunnathu Mathew (later Malankara Metropolitan Mathews Mar Athanasius) was also present on this historic occasion.Syrian Christians from surrounding hamlets—including Mallappally, Keezhvaipur, Murani, Anicadu, and Punnavely—enrolled as parishioners, with families actively contributing personal labour and resources to the church's erection. Following an initial period when visiting priests ministered to the congregation, construction was realized through the sacrificial leadership of two consecutive vicars from the Vazhayil family. The first vicar, Rev. Isaac Kathanar (ordained 1840–41 AD [1016 ME]), resided on the grounds in a makeshift shed for five years, personally supervising the stonework before his passing in 1848–49 AD [1024 ME]. His nephew and successor, Rev. Varghese Isaac Kathanar (ordained 1857–58 AD [1033 ME]), completed the remaining carpentry and led the parish until his death in 1867–68 AD [1043 ME]. Both priests dedicated their full earnings to the sanctuary and lie buried side by side within the church nave (haikkala), beside the baptismal font. Subsequently, Rev. 1956 ജൂലൈ മാസം 8ാം തീയതി മലങ്കര ഓർത്തോഡോക്സ് സുറിയാനി സഭയുടെ നിരണം ഭദ്രാസനത്തിൻ്റെ കീഴിൽ സ്ഥാപിതമായ ദേവാലയമാണ് തിരുവൻവണ്ടൂർ സെൻ്റ് ജോർജ്ജ് ഓർത്തഡോക്സ് പള്ളി. നിരണം ഭദ്രാസനത്തിൻ്റെ മെത്രാപ്പോലീത്ത ആയിരുന്ന അഭിവന്ദ്യ തോമാ മാർ ദിവന്യാസിയോസ് മെത്രാപ്പോലീത്തായുടെയും, തോട്ടത്തിൽ വീട്ടിൽ ഗീവർഗീസ് അച്ചൻ്റെയും, മറ്റ്‌ വിശ്വാസികളുടെയും പ്രയത്‌നഭലമായി രൂപം കൊണ്ട ദേവാലയമാണ് കൊച്ചുപള്ളി എന്ന് അറിയപ്പെടുന്ന ഈ ദേവാലയം.

ഇതര ക്രിസ്തീയ സഭകളിൽ നിന്നുള്ള സാമ്പത്തിക സഹായ വാഗ്ദാനം മൂലം ഉമയാറ്റുകര സെൻ്റ് തോമസ് പള്ളിയിൽ ഇടവകാംഗങ്ങളായ തിരുവൻവണ്ടൂരിലെ ഭൂരിപക്ഷം ജനങ്ങളും തങ്ങളുടെ ഓർത്തഡോക്സ്‌ വിശ്വാസം ഉപേക്ഷിച്ച് മറ്റ് സഭാവിശ്വാസം സ്വീകരിക്കുന്നതിനിടയായി. ഇതുമൂലം ഉണ്ടായ വിശ്വാസികളുടെ കൊഴിഞ്ഞുപോക്ക്, ഒരു പുതിയ ദേവാലയം പണിയുവാൻ അഭിവന്ദ്യ തോമാ മാർ ദിവന്യാസിയോസ് മെത്രാപ്പോലീത്തക്കും, ഗീവർഗീസ് അച്ചനും പ്രേരണയായി.

ഓർത്തഡോക്സ് വിശ്വാസം ത്യജിക്കാതെ നിലനിന്നിരുന്ന വിശ്വാസികൾക്ക് ആശ്വാസദായകമയി അവർക്കായി ഒരു ചെറിയ പള്ളി പണിയുവാനുള്ള സ്ഥലം വാങ്ങുകയും, അതിൽ ഓലമേഞ്ഞ ഷെഡ് കെട്ടി 1956 ജൂലൈ മാസം 8-ാം തീയതി പ്രഥമബലി അർപ്പിക്കുകയും ചെയ്തു. തിരുമേനിയുടെ കല്പനപ്രകാരം 1957 ജൂലൈ 11 മുതൽ ബഹു. തോട്ടത്തിൽ വീട്ടിൽ ഗീവർഗ്ഗീസ് അച്ചനെ വികാരിയായി നിയമിച്ചു. ഉമയാറ്റുകര പള്ളിയുടെ ചാപ്പലായി വി. ഗീവർഗ്ഗീസ് സഹദായുടെ നാമത്തിൽ ഈ ചെറിയ ദേവാലയം തിരുമേനിയുടെ കല്പനയാൽ പ്രഖ്യാപിച്ചു.

തോട്ടത്തിൽ വീട്ടിൽ ഗീവർഗ്ഗീസ് അച്ചൻ്റെ കാലശേഷം അദ്ദേഹത്തിൻ്റെ മകനായ റ്റി. ജി. സഖറിയ അച്ചൻ 1971 മുതൽ സഹവികാരിയും, പിന്നീട് വികാരിയുമായി ഭരണം നിർവഹിക്കുകയും, ഇടവകയ്ക് സ്വന്തമായി ഒരു ഇടവക കല്ലറപണിയിക്കുകയും, പള്ളി വിപുലീകരിക്കുകയും, മാസത്തിൽ എല്ലാ ഞായറാഴ്ചയും വി. കുർബാനയുള്ള സ്വതന്ത്ര ഇടവകയാക്കുകയും ചെയ്തു. 1993 വരെ അച്ചൻ ഈ ഇടവകയിൽ സ്തുത്യാർഹമായ സേവനമനുഷ്ഠിച്ചു. തുടർന്നുവന്ന വൈദീകരുടെയും, ഇടവക ജനങ്ങളുടെയും പ്രവർത്തനഭലമായി ഇടവക പുരോഗമന വീഥിയിൽ കൂടി നാളിതുവരെ ദൈവകൃപയാൽ കടന്നുപോയി. കൊച്ചുപള്ളി എന്ന് അറിയപ്പെടുന്ന ഈ ദേവാലയം ഇന്ന് തിരുവൻവണ്ടൂറിലെ ജനങ്ങൾക് ഒരു ആശ്രയ കേന്ദ്രമാണ്.

ഓർത്തഡോക്സ്‌ വൈദീക സെമിനാരിയിലെ സീനിയർ അദ്യാപകനായ റവ. ഫാ. ഡോ. നൈനാൻ കെ. ജോർജ്ജ് 2019 മുതൽ ഈ ഇടവകയിൽ വികാരിയായി സേവനം അനുഷ്ഠിച്ചുവരുന്നു. നടപ്പുസാമ്പത്തിക വർഷം ഇടവക ട്രസ്റ്റിയായി ലിജു ഏബ്രഹാം സേവനം അനുഷ്ഠിക്കുന്നു.

ds: A protected heritage site in Parumala, Kerala, this historic seminary building stands on the banks of the Pamba River and served as the original residence of Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios (Parumala Thirumeni). Established after Malankara Metropolitan Pulikkottil Joseph Mar Dionysius V sought to found a regional seminary, it was built on a two-acre site donated by Arikupurathu Mathen Karnavar. Initially a modest thatched structure, it became the birthplace of Malankara Orthodox ministerial training, where deacons studied Syriac and theology. The saint lived alongside trainees, overseeing their formation and church administration, helping lay the foundations for diocesan leadership, ministerial development, and missionary work. It remains an important preserved landmark.

186 families (2026) 

St. John’s Bethany Orthodox Valiyapally stands as an eminent sanctuary in the heart of Mallappally town, along the banks of the Manimala River in the Pathanamthitta district of Keralam. Falling under the Mallappally ecclesiastical district of the historic Niranam Diocese, the parish holds a prominent place in the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church as the mother parish of Saint Geevarghese Mar Dionysius of Vattasseril (Malankara Sabha Bhasuran), the second canonised saint of the Church.

History:
The spiritual roots of the parish trace back to Vengalasserry St. Mary’s Old Syrian Church (Kaattupally), established atop Vengalasserry Hill on 13 July 1834 AD [29 Midhunam 1009 ME] to serve the faithful of Mallappally who had previously journeyed to the ancient church in Kallooppara. Following the 19th-century church reformation, Vengalasserry Church became one of only five sanctuaries in Keralam shared equally between the Orthodox and Mar Thoma communities. Preserving this enduring sacred bond, the liturgical services and spiritual ministrations at Vengalasserry Church continue to be conducted under the pastoral care of St. John’s Bethany Orthodox Valiyapally.
Worship at the hill-top church had faced disruption in 1918–19 AD [1094 ME], when a shortage of priests and the hardships of crossing the river prompted the faithful to seek an accessible town-side sanctuary. Securing the pastoral care of Rev. Philipose Kathanar of Ayroor Chembothara, the faithful acquired one acre of land from the Mannathu Nair family at Otharakunnel on the western bank of the Manimala River. A temporary shed was erected, a cross set up, and the Holy Qurbana commenced in January 1920 AD [Makaram 1095 ME], celebrated by Rev. Fr. Chakkupurackal of Vakathanam. Owing to its location on the hillock, the church came to be popularly known among the local community as Otharakunnupally. Following a brief four-week suspension of services due to local disputes, regular worship was permanently restored through the decisive intervention of Saint Geevarghese Mar Dionysius of Vattasseril.
Rev. Varghese David Kathanar of Payyampallil (Payyampallil Vallyachan) served as the first vicar. Following his death in 1104 ME, he was buried in the church. Pastoral charge then passed to Rev. Philipose Kathanar of Vattasseril Thoppil (Thoppil Achan), who had previously served as vicar and manager of Parumala Seminary for nearly twenty-five years and would lead the parish devotedly for approximately two decades. During this era, with formal sanction secured from the Quilon Peishkar, Mr C. K. Matthen, plans were formulated for a permanent church. This period coincided with the ecclesiastical crisis following the Full Bench verdict of 24 March 1923 AD [10 Meenam 1098 ME], which overturned the decree of 15 September 1919 AD [30 Chingam 1095 ME] and threatened parish properties across Malankara. Guided by the strategic vision of Saint Geevarghese Mar Dionysius to secure congregations under dedicated "Bethany" churches, the cornerstone for the permanent sanctuary was laid by the Saint on 20 January 1929 AD [7 Makaram 1104 ME]. The building was completed through his personal benefaction and the sacrificial contributions of the faithful. Following the demise of Saint Geevarghese Mar Dionysius on 23 February 1934 AD [11 Kumbham 1109 ME], the parish perpetuated his memory by establishing a roadside shrine (Kurishumthotti) on church property in Mallappally market.
In 1958, advanced age led Rev. Fr. Philipose of Thoppil to retire five years prior to his passing, handing over parish administration to Rev. Fr. P. M. Abraham of Payyampallil. During Father Abraham's tenure, a dedicated building was constructed on the northern grounds to accommodate the Sunday School and parish office. Following his sudden demise on 5 December 1971, he was laid to rest in a specially prepared tomb within the church grounds. Thereafter, the liturgical and pastoral needs of the parish were administered

n: Kadampanad St. Thomas Orthodox Cathedral & Historic Thomasine Pilgrim Centre
ds:
Established by migrants from Nilackal in 325 CE in the name of St. Thomas. Rebuilt in 800, 1200, 1800, 1912, 1952 CE. The church additionally grew in members from Nilackal refugees in the 12th and 14th centuries. This church has hundreds of daughter parishes, notably those at: Mavelikkara, Kayamkulam, Kollakadavu, Adoor, Kozhencherry, Kaipattoor, Sooranad, Kallada and Koodal. St. Gregorios of Parumala had a grand apostolic visit to this church in 1895.

Mar Thoma III of Kadampanad is entombed in the altar of this church.

The parish was declared a Marthoman Pilgrim Centre on 7 March 2010 by the Catholicos.

25 families (2022) – Situated in the rural village of Parasuvaikkal, approximately 300 meters from the Kerala–Tamil Nadu border, this church serves one of the southernmost Orthodox congregations in the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese.

Despite its small size, the parish maintains a vibrant Orthodox presence in this remote region. At least one priest of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church has come from this parish, reflecting its contribution to the life of the Church beyond its modest congregation.
Cemetery Chapel of the Nearby Parish.

400 families (2022) – With a history spanning more than 160 years, this is one of the oldest and most historically significant parishes of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese. Before a church existed in the region, the ascetic priest Younan Kaseesha, affectionately remembered as Anchal Achan, ministered to the Orthodox faithful while serving from Kottarakkara. As Christian families migrated to Anchal for agriculture, trade, and employment, the growing community established a simple thatched chapel dedicated to St. George on the Kandathil property, creating the first permanent Orthodox place of worship in the area.

Recognizing the need for a permanent church, community leaders petitioned the Malankara Metropolitan for permission to build a parish. In 1903, a church was erected on nearly one acre of land generously donated by the prominent advocate Elanjikkal Cherian Chacko (Varinjam Sir), together with the efforts of Changampallil Koruthu Vadyar and Mathai Mathunni. Rev. Fr. Abraham of Kundara Thenguvila became the first vicar, and the parish soon developed into the principal Orthodox church of the Anchal region.

The present church was consecrated in 1985 by H.G. Geevarghese Mar Dioscoros, the founding Metropolitan of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese, assisted by H.G. Geevarghese Mar Osthathios. Continued growth led to the construction of a meditation room dedicated to Anchal Achan (1990), a meditation hall and church porch (1998), a new clergy residence (2002), the Anchal Achan Memorial Parish Hall (2007), and a granite cross with landscaped entrance consecrated by H.G. Dr. Gabriel Mar Gregorios in 2013.

The parish maintains three prominent roadside shrines dedicated to St. George. The first was established along the Ayur–Anchal Road in 1965 on land donated by the late Mr. Krishnan Muthalali. A second shrine was constructed on the Anchal–Punalur Road in 1996 on land donated by the late Mr. E. John of the Elavukattu family. The third shrine was erected in 2005 along the Kadakkal–Chengamanad Road by the Punalur Changampallil family on land donated by the children of the late Mr. C. T. Samuel. A ceremonial flagmast sponsored by the Punalur Changampallil family was added to the church campus in 2009.

Recognizing its historical and spiritual importance, H.G. Dr. Gabriel Mar Gregorios proclaimed the parish as St. George Orthodox Valiyapally in 2009. On June 13, 2010, H.H. Baselios Marthoma Didymos I declared it a Georgian Pilgrimage Centre, acknowledging its importance as one of southern Kerala's principal centers of devotion to St. George.

Today, the parish serves more than 1,600 faithful across five panchayats—Anchal, Edamulakkal, Alayamon, Karavaloor, and Ittiva—and functions as the Mother Church of the region. Organized into eleven wards with seven active prayer groups, it sustains vibrant Sunday School, youth, women's, and spiritual organizations while maintaining extensive charitable ministries that provide assistance for housing, education, marriages, and medical needs regardless of caste or religion. The annual feasts of St. George and the revered Anchal Achan continue to attract large numbers of pilgrims from across southern Kerala.

475 families (2022) – Established around 1755, this is one of the oldest Orthodox churches in southern Kerala and the oldest church in Chathannoor. Historically known as "Chathannoor Marthamariyam Suriyani Pally," it became the Mother Church of the Chathannoor region, from which numerous Orthodox parishes were later established. Today, it remains one of the largest parishes in the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese.

The church preserves an exceptional collection of historical artifacts spanning more than two centuries. Among its most treasured works is a rare 1792 mural of St. George, depicting the saint from an uncommon perspective unlike the traditional dragon-slaying iconography. The church also houses the historic Chathannoor Panchangam, written in both Malayalam and Tamil, which preserves important records of the Malankara Church and references to Mar Nicholas's visit to Kerala.

Another remarkable artifact is an 1861 painting by British Army Lieutenant Colonel Stevenson portraying Geevarghese Yacob Kattanar celebrating the Holy Qurbana while offering his sword, providing a rare visual record of nineteenth-century Malankara liturgical life. The church has also carefully preserved ancient stone lamps, candlestands, and other liturgical objects despite successive renovations. A massive stone oil lamp carved from a single block of granite still stands before the entrance and continues to attract devotees from different faiths who light lamps there in prayer.

More than two and a half centuries after its founding, the church remains one of the foremost centers of Orthodox worship and heritage in southern Kerala, preserving the liturgical, artistic, and historical traditions of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.

n: Kodunganoor St. Gregorios Orthodox Mission Centre
ds:
Established under the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church in the name of St. Gregorios of Parumala, this rehabilitation center provides comprehensive support for economically disadvantaged persons with disabilities through institution-based care and community outreach.

The center conducts surveys to identify individuals in need, provides counseling, facilitates medical treatment, corrective surgeries, physiotherapy, prosthetic devices, and other rehabilitation services, and promotes disability prevention through public awareness programs.

It also supports economic independence by offering financial assistance, small-business loans, and vocational training, including tailoring, electronics repair, and other practical skills, enabling persons with disabilities to achieve greater self-sufficiency.

The parish received widespread attention following an Onam celebration held inside the church that featured a performer portraying Mahabali, sparking significant public controversy and discussion within sections of the Orthodox community.

431 families (2022) – Established as a filial parish of the Palayam Cathedral, this church serves one of the larger Orthodox congregations in Thiruvananthapuram.

Despite its size, the church accommodates only about 350 worshippers at a time—roughly 17% of its approximately 2,100 members—with additional capacity available during major feast days. Attendance is highest during weddings, baptisms, funerals, Christmas, Good Friday, and Easter.

For many years, the parish was shepherded by Very Rev. Fr. Alexander Vaidyan Cor-Episcopa, who served as its longest-tenured vicar.

Situated on one of the highest elevations around Thiruvananthapuram, this cemetery and chapel serve the burial needs of Thekkan Parumala St. Peter's & St. Paul's Orthodox Church.

Its hilltop setting provides sweeping views of the surrounding landscape, making it one of the region's most scenic Orthodox cemeteries. Access is by a steep uphill road, which can become difficult for low-clearance vehicles, particularly during the monsoon season.

The cemetery chapel continues to host funeral services, memorial prayers, and other liturgical observances for the parish community.

Established as the cemetery chapel of St. Thomas Orthodox Church, Kumarapuram, this chapel serves the parish burial grounds at Malamukal.

Located on the outskirts of Thiruvananthapuram, the cemetery was developed after affordable land became available on the surrounding hilltops, providing space for future burials beyond the increasingly land-constrained city.

The chapel continues to serve funeral services, memorial prayers, and other liturgical observances associated with the parish cemetery.

378 families (2025), 521 families (2022) – Originally established as a filial chapel of the Palayam Cathedral, this church has developed into one of the major Orthodox parishes in the eastern part of Thiruvananthapuram.

The parish traces its beginnings to a chapel established to serve the Orthodox students and staff of the nearby Mar Ivanios College. Today, it continues to uphold this legacy of faith and learning while expanding into a vibrant parish community.

Serving approximately 1,812 faithful across six parish wards, the church remains an important center of worship, pastoral care, and community life for Orthodox families in the rapidly growing Nalanchira region. The parish is presently served by two priests, ensuring regular liturgical services and pastoral ministry for the faithful.

The church enshrines the Holy Relics of Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios (Parumala Thirumeni), making it a place of particular spiritual significance.

Before the present church was constructed, the site functioned as an active diocesan youth development center. Today, the parish celebrates the Holy Qurbana every Sunday from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m., followed by breakfast for the faithful.

n: Palavilai St. George Tamil Orthodox Church
ds:
85 families (2022) – This mission church serves the Tamil Orthodox community of Palavilai and is one of the principal centers of the Malankara Orthodox mission among the ethnic Tamil population of Kanyakumari.

All liturgical services, prayers, and parish activities are conducted in Tamil, reflecting the linguistic and cultural heritage of the congregation.

105 students (2025) – Established in 1975 under the leadership of L.L. H.G. Philipose Mar Theophilos, this MGOCSM center became a pioneering model for Orthodox student ministry in Kerala.

Its first warden, Rev. Dn. George Kurien, later H.G. Geevarghese Mar Coorilos, transformed a repurposed residence into a dedicated center for student life and spiritual formation.

Today, the center continues to serve Orthodox students through residential accommodation, theological formation, and community life, remaining one of the flagship institutions of the MGOCSM.

Consecrated in 1977 by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews I, this chapel forms the spiritual heart of the MGOCSM center in Thiruvananthapuram.

The consecration of the expanded complex, including the chapel, auditorium, and guest facilities, was attended by international ecumenical representatives, reflecting its significance within Orthodox student ministry.

The chapel continues to host regular worship and serves as a center for the liturgical and spiritual life of Orthodox students.

Established in 1975 during a period of ecclesiastical realignment, this church emerged as a distinct Patriarchal congregation in Thiruvananthapuram. Its present church was consecrated on February 13–14, 1982, by Patriarch Ignatius Zakka I Iwas and has since been administered under the 1979 Patriarchal constitution.

The parish serves more than 250 families and oversees several charitable institutions, including a special-needs school, two cemeteries, and a cross shrine at Pongumoodu, which was elevated to parish status in 2003.

Its first leader was a lay acolyte ordained to the priesthood within four months without formal seminary formation, a decision widely criticized as a significant departure from established ecclesiastical discipline.

n: Parottukonam St. Thomas Karunya Monastery & Convent
ds:
This monastery and convent serves as a center of prayer, monastic life, and charitable ministry under the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church. A Ramban resides here alongside monks and nuns who oversee the institution's spiritual and social outreach.

The complex houses the St. Thomas Karunya Guidance Centre and serves as the administrative center for Karunya Vishranti Bhavan, a palliative care center, an old-age home, the Karunya Snehabhojanam food assistance program, the Karunya Sick Aid Foundation, and a marriage assistance foundation. Together, these ministries provide healthcare, financial assistance, and compassionate support to vulnerable members of society.

This chapel forms part of the St. Thomas Karunya Guidance Centre, serving as the spiritual heart of the monastery's charitable ministries and providing regular liturgical services for its residents, staff, and the surrounding Orthodox community.

The foundation stone was laid on August 24, 1986, by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews I, Catholicos of the East and Malankara Metropolitan, marking the beginning of the center's spiritual and charitable mission.

Located on prime land in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram, this cemetery is the historic burial ground of the Palayam Cathedral and contains more than 5,000 interments.

Having reached full capacity, most new burials are now conducted at Malamukal. Families with relatives already interred here, however, may continue to use existing family burial plots.

A weekly service is held every Saturday at the Pattoor Cemetery Chapel, with Morning Prayer at 6:30 a.m. followed by the Holy Qurbana at 7:00 a.m.

60 families (2022) – This church is the first in Kerala and the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church to be dedicated to Saint Dionysius, giving it a unique place in the church's history.

Sunday Holy Mass is celebrated starting at 06:30 AM.

Though presently a small parish, it continues to grow and has long been envisioned as a future pilgrimage center dedicated to the legacy of the saint. Expansion of the church and its facilities remains a long-term objective.

Established under the Palayam Cathedral, this shrine was built to serve the Orthodox faithful of the Plammoodu area.

It was founded as a votive offering by a parishioner who credited St. George with saving his life after a snakebite. The shrine also enshrines icons of the Virgin Mary and Jesus Christ, making it a place of prayer and devotion for the local community.

n: Pooyappally St. Peter's and St. Paul's Orthodox Church
ds: 95 families (2022)

Located in the rural outskirts north of Thiruvananthapuram, this monastery serves as a center of Orthodox monastic life, prayer, and spiritual formation. The peaceful setting provides an environment well suited for silent prayer and contemplation while preserving the ascetic traditions of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church in Kerala's capital region.

The monastery is home to several religious brothers (celibate priests). It also serves as the present residence of H.G. Gabriel Mar Gregorios, Metropolitan of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese, making it an important spiritual center of the diocese.

n: Sreekariyam Holy Cross Convent & St. George Orthodox Chapel (Alathara)
ds:
This convent serves as a center of prayer, monastic life, and Christian service under the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church. The resident sisters oversee the adjoining St. George Orthodox Chapel while carrying out ministries of education, worship, and community outreach.

The convent also administers Holy Trinity English Medium Higher Secondary School, one of the major educational institutions of the Thiruvananthapuram Orthodox Diocese, continuing the Church's longstanding commitment to academic excellence and Christian values.

is chapel serves as the spiritual center of the St. Thomas Karunya Monastery and Karunya Vishranti Bhavan, providing daily worship for the monastery's resident clergy, religious, and approximately 50 inmates of the care home.

Regular evening prayers are conducted every day, while Holy Qurbana is celebrated on Sundays.

n: Sreekariyam St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory Orthodox Church
ds:
251 families (2022) – Established as an independent parish in 1985, this church traces its origins to a congregation formed in 1978 by families of the Palayam St. George Orthodox Cathedral who had settled in the Sreekariyam area.

Before the parish was established, the faithful gathered for prayer in their homes while a temporary building at the present site served as both a Sunday School and place of worship. H.G. Geevarghese Mar Dioscoros formally established the parish on July 17, 1985, dedicating it to the Cappadocian Fathers, St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory.

The present church was constructed and consecrated on February 3–4, 2000, by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews II, Catholicos of the East and Malankara Metropolitan. Today, it continues to serve as one of the principal Orthodox parishes in northern Thiruvananthapuram.

This monastery serves as a center of Orthodox monastic life and charitable ministry under the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church. Home to a resident monk and nun, it oversees Karunya Vishranti Bhavan, a major humanitarian institution established in 1998 to provide compassionate care for the poor, the sick, and the abandoned.

The campus offers hospice and palliative care for terminally ill cancer patients, residential care for elderly and homeless individuals, psychosocial rehabilitation for people with mental illness, support for those living with HIV/AIDS, a primary healthcare clinic, and a day-care program for the local poor. Patients and residents are provided accommodation, meals, medical assistance, counseling, and spiritual care regardless of caste, religion, or social background.

n: Thiruvithamcode St. Mary's Malankara Orthodox Church
ds:
12 families (2022) - Traditionally believed to have been consecrated by Saint Thomas the Apostle in AD 63, this church is revered as one of the Ezharappallikal (Seven and a Half Churches) established during his missionary journey after arriving in India around AD 52. It remains one of the oldest and most significant centers of St. Thomas Christian heritage.

Known as Arappally or Thomayar Kovil, the church is traditionally called the "Half Church" because Saint Thomas is believed to have initially established only a cross or simple place of prayer for the first Christian families. Another tradition associates the name with a "Royal Church," reflecting the patronage of the King of Venad, who granted land for its construction.

Unlike most ancient churches of India, this church preserves much of its original architectural character. Constructed from locally quarried granite blocks, it incorporates features common to early South Indian temple architecture, including granite pillars, wooden foyers, terracotta roofing, and a sanctuary resembling the traditional Sreekovil. Among its surviving antiquities are an ancient baptismal font, a Portuguese hanging lamp, a historic censer, a two-thousand-year-old well that has never run dry, and a stone cross traditionally attributed to Saint Thomas.

For nearly two millennia, this church has remained a continuous place of Christian worship and is traditionally regarded as one of the oldest church structures in the world still holding daily prayers. It is maintained by the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church and was proclaimed an International St. Thomas Pilgrimage Centre on December 16, 2007, by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Didymos I.

According to local tradition, the early Christian community endured severe persecution after its establishment. A woman remembered as Chirutha is said to have organized a force known as the Chirutha Pada to defend the newly converted Christians, becoming a lasting figure in the region's Christian heritage.

Today, the church remains one of the foremost pilgrimage destinations of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, drawing thousands of pilgrims, historians, and visitors each year to one of the most historically significant Christian sites in India.

Commonly known as Holy Trinity Church, Ulloor, it functions much like a parish church, providing regular liturgical services and pastoral care.

The chapel is also home to Holy Trinity Media, an Orthodox media ministry that supports the Church's evangelistic and educational outreach through digital and multimedia initiatives.

Since 1986, this Orthodox Center has served as the official episcopal residence of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese.

Established through the vision of H.G. Geevarghese Mar Dioscoros, the center occupies a central location in Ulloor while providing a peaceful setting for prayer, administration, and diocesan ministry. It continues to function as an important administrative and spiritual hub of the diocese.

n: Sooranad North St. Mary's Orthodox Shrine
Sooranad North St. Mary's Salem Orthodox Church
ds:
81 families (2022) - The Orthodox faithful residing in and around Sooranad North, particularly near the Government High School and Kannamam Market area, were for many years members of their mother parishes—St. Thomas Orthodox Church and St. Mary's Orthodox Church, Sooranad. Due to the difficulty of travelling long distances to attend Holy Qurbana and other liturgical services, the need for a new parish gradually became evident. A plot of land, adjacent to St. Thomas U.P. School, owned by the Church, was graciously made available. After obtaining the necessary permissions, construction of the new church was initiated by dismantling an old structure within the school premises.

On 22 November 1968, under the leadership Fr. T.G. Geevarghese, the faithful formally entered the church premises. The foundation stone of the church was laid on 28 November 1968. The parish was officially established in January 1969. The consecration ceremonies were completed on 30 and 31 January 1969. Rev. Fr. T. G. Geevarghese was appointed as the first Vicar, and the parish was named St. Mary's Salem Orthodox Syrian Church, Sooranad North. Subsequently, the parish committee and various spiritual organizations were formed. From February 1969 onward, regular Holy Qurbana and worship services were conducted.

1,916 families (2022) – Consecrated in 1900 by Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios (Parumala Thirumeni) in the presence of Malankara Metropolitan Mar Joseph Dionysius, this church became the first Syrian Christian parish established in the Thiruvananthapuram district. It later gave rise to the region's subsequent Malankara Orthodox, Mar Thoma, Malankara Catholic, and Jacobite communities, making it one of the most historically influential parishes in the capital.

On June 23, 1991, H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews II elevated it to cathedral status as the episcopal seat of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese. Today, it is the largest urban parish in the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, with more than 9,000 regularly attending parishioners.

The parish celebrates four weekly Holy Qurbanas, three additional monthly services, and maintains thirteen active prayer organizations. Its annual feast of St. George draws thousands of devotees, while the cathedral's blend of traditional Kerala and Byzantine architecture, murals, icons, and carved wooden interior reflects the artistic heritage of the Malankara Church.

Among its notable members is renowned playback singer K. J. Yesudas, who was married at this church.

Established in 2004, this mission center is home to the Mar Dioscorus College of Pharmacy, a flagship educational institution of the Charitable and Educational Society of the Thiruvananthapuram Orthodox Diocese. Named in honor of H.G. Geevarghese Mar Dioscoros, the Diocese's founding Metropolitan, it reflects the Church's commitment to higher education and professional formation.

Affiliated with the Kerala University of Health Sciences, the college offers Diploma in Pharmacy (D.Pharm), Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm), Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D), Master of Pharmacy (M.Pharm), and Ph.D. programs. It serves as one of the leading Orthodox educational institutions in Kerala, combining academic excellence with the values of Christian service and ethical healthcare.

Established in 1987, this Orthodox center serves as one of the principal spiritual gathering places of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese.

The center hosts the annual Trivandrum Orthodox Convention, bringing together clergy and faithful each year for worship, preaching, and spiritual renewal. It remains an important venue for diocesan conventions and major ecclesiastical events.

പരിശുദ്ധ പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ തിരുശേഷിപ്പിനാൽ ധന്യമായ ആഗോള പൗരസ്ത്യ ജോർജ്ജിയൻ തീർത്ഥാടന കേന്ദ്രം:

എ.ഡി 1915 ഒക്ടോബര്‍ മാസത്തില്‍ ബഥേല്‍ സെന്റ്‌ ജോര്‍ജ്ജ്‌ പള്ളി എന്ന നാമധേയത്തില്‍ ദേവാലയത്തിന്റെ പണി തുടങ്ങി 1916 ജനുവരി മാസത്തില്‍ ദേവാലയത്തിന്റെ കൂദാശാ കര്‍മ്മം കാലം ചെയ്‌ത ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ ദ്വിതീയന്‍ കാതോലിക്കാ ബാവാ തിരുമേനി നടത്തി. പ്രസ്തുത ദേവാലയം 1919 ജൂലൈ മാസത്തില്‍ ഉണ്ടായ കാറ്റും മഴയും മൂലം ഇടിഞ്ഞുവീണു. പെട്ടെന്ന്‌ അതേ സ്ഥാനത്ത്‌ തന്നെ ദൈവാലയം പണിതു.

പുതിയ മദ്ബഹായുടെ പണി 1952 ഒക്ടോബര്‍ മാസത്തില്‍ ആരംഭിച്ചു. അതിന്റെ ഉത്തരനിരപ്പു വരെയുള്ള കെട്ട്‌ 1963-ല്‍ പൂര്‍ത്തിയായി. ഈ ഭിത്തി 12-7-1963-ല്‍ ഉണ്ടായ അതിഭയങ്കരമായ മഴ നിമിത്തം ഇടിഞ്ഞു വീഴുകയുണ്ടായി. വീണ്ടും അതേ പ്ലാനില്‍ തന്നെ ഒരു മദ്ബഹാ പണിയണമെന്നുള്ള പൊതു യോഗ തീരുമാനമനുസരിച്ച്‌ 22-8-1963-ല്‍ റവ, വൈദ്യന്‍ യോശുവ കത്തനാര്‍ അവര്‍കളാല്‍ ശിലാസ്ഥാപനം നടത്തപ്പെടുകയും തുടര്‍ന്ന്‌ പണി നടത്തപ്പെടുകയും ചെയ്തു 1971-ല്‍ പുതിയ പള്ളിയുടെ പണി ആരംഭിച്ചു. പുതിയ ദേവാലയത്തിന്‌ പോര്‍ച്ച്‌ ഉള്‍പ്പടെ 90 അടിനീളവും 27 അടി വീതിയുമുണ്ട്‌. ദേവാലയത്തിന്റെ കൂദാശ 1985 ജനുവരി 9, 10 തീയതികളില്‍ മോറോന്‍ മാര്‍ ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ മാര്‍ത്തോമ്മ മാത്യൂസ്‌ പ്രഥമന്‍ കാതോലിക്കാ ബാവായുടെ പ്രധാന കാര്‍മ്മികത്വത്തിലും, മോറോന്‍ മാര്‍ ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ മാര്‍ത്തോമ്മ മാത്യൂസ്‌ ദ്വിതീയന്‍ കതോലിക്കാ ബാവയുടേയും (അന്ന്‌ നിയുക്ത കാതോലിക്കാ), അഭി.ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ലീസ്‌ മാര്‍ ദീയസ്‌കോറസ്‌ തിരുമേനിയുടെ സഹകരണത്തിലും നടത്തി.

ദൈവാലയത്തിന്റെ സ്ഥലപരിമിതി മനസ്സിലാക്കി ഇരുവശങ്ങള്‍ വീതി കൂട്ടുകയും, അതിനോടനുബന്ധിച്ച്‌ രണ്ട്‌ മദ്ബഹാകള്‍ നിര്‍മ്മിക്കുകയും ചെയ്തു, കുര്‍ബാന അനുഷ്ഠിക്കുവാന്‍ 5 ബലി പീഠങ്ങളുമുണ്ട്‌.

പരിശുദ്ധ ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ സഹദായുടെ അതിശ്രേഷ്ഠമായ മദ്ധ്യസ്ഥതയുള്ള ഈ ദൈവാലയത്തെ, പൗരസ്ത്യ കാതോലിക്കായും, മലങ്കര മെത്രാ പോലീത്തയുമായ മോറോന്‍ മാര്‍ ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ മര്‍ത്തോമ്മ പൗലോസ്‌ ദ്വിതീയന്‍ തിരുമനസ്സുകൊണ്ട്‌ നമ്പർ 39/2011 കല്പന പ്രകാരം നല്ലില സെന്റ് ജോർജ് ഓർത്തഡോക്സ് തീർത്ഥാടന പള്ളി എന്ന പേരിൽ ജോർജ്ജിയൻ തീർത്ഥാടന കേന്ദ്രമായി ഉയർത്തപെട്ടു. 2011 മെയ്‌ 2-ാം തീയതി തീർത്ഥാടന പ്രഖ്യാപനം സമ്മേളനം നടത്തപ്പെട്ടു.

പരിശുദ്ധ എപ്പിസ്‌ക്കോപ്പന്‍ സുന്നഹദോസ്‌ ഇടവകയുടെ അപേക്ഷ പരിഗണിച്ച്‌ നമ്പര്‍ HES/HH/75/2011 കല്പന പ്രകാരം നവംബര്‍ മാസം 11-ാം തീയതി പരിശുദ്ധ പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ തിരു ശേഷിപ്പ് അഭിവന്ദ്യ സഖറിയാ മാര്‍ അന്തോണിയോസ്‌ മെത്രാപൊലീത്താ തിരുമനസ്സിന്റേയും അഭിവന്ദ്യ പൗലോസ്‌ മാര്‍ പക്കോമിയോസ്‌ തിരുമനസ്സിന്റേയും പ്രധാന കാര്‍മ്മികത്വത്തില്‍ പ്രതിഷ്ഠിക്കുകയുണ്ടായി എല്ലാ മാസവും 2-ാം ശനിയാഴ്ച ജോര്‍ജജിയന്‍ ധ്യാനവും എല്ലാ 4-ാം ശനിയാഴ്ച സന്ധ്യ നമസ്ക്കാരത്തിനു ശേഷം പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ നാമത്തിൽ മദ്ധ്യസ്ഥ പ്രാര്‍ത്ഥനയും നടത്തുന്നു.

ഇപ്പോൾ ഈ ദൈവാലയത്തിൽ 435 ഭവനങ്ങൾ ഉണ്ട്. 12 കുരിശടികളും, ഒരേക്കർ 34 സെന്റ് വസ്തു വും, പള്ളിയോട് ചേർന്ന് ഒരു പാഴ്സനേജും ഉണ്ട്. പള്ളിയുടെ ചുമതലയിൽ ബഥേൽ ഇംഗ്ലീഷ് മീഡിയം സ്കൂൾ എന്ന പേരിൽ ഒരു സ്കൂളും പ്രവർത്തിച്ചു വരുന്നു. സഭയിലെ എല്ലാ ആത്മീയ സംഘടനകളും, ഇടവകയിലെ ഭവനങ്ങളെ 8 വാർഡുകളായി വിഭജിച്ച് പ്രാർഥനായോഗങ്ങളും നടന്നുവരുന്നു. ഇപ്പോൾ ഇടവകയിൽ 5 പട്ടക്കാരും മരുമക്കളായ 5 പട്ടക്കാരും ഉണ്ട്. ഫാ. ഗീവർഗ്ഗീസ്, മത്തായി, ഫാ. വി.കെ. ഡാനിയേൽ, ഫാ. , ജോഷം വൈദ്യൻ, ഫാ. പി.എം. ജോർജ്ജ്, അലക്സാണ്ടർ, ഫാ. എം. തോമസുകുട്ടി, ഫാ. സ്റ്റീഫൻ വൈരമൺ, ഫാ. ഫിലിപ്പ് മാത്യു, ഫാ. റെജി ലൂക്കോസ്, ഫാ. കെ. കെ. തോമസ്, ഫാ. വർഗ്ഗീസ് കോശി, ഫാ. ജേക്കബ് ജോർജ്, ഫാ. ജേക്കബ് പണിക്കർ, സജീവ് വർഗ്ഗീസ്, ഫാ.വി.ജി കോശി വൈദ്യൻ, ഫാ.ജോസ് എം ദാനിയേൽ, ഫാ.ജോൺ പണിക്കർ കോർ എപ്പിസ്കോപ്പ,ഫാ. മാത്യൂ എബ്രഹാം തലവൂർ എന്നിവർ വികാരിമാരായിരുന്നു. ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ വികാരിയായി ഫാ ബേസിൽ ജെ പണിക്കർ സേവനമനുഷ്ടിക്കുന്നു.

n: Thenmala Junction St. George Orthodox Shrine
ds: Thenmala St. George Orthodox Church

Dedicated to Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios (Parumala Thirumeni), this roadside shrine was established on land donated by Mr. P. S. Rajappan, who gifted approximately four cents of property to the parish for the erection of a granite cross.

The shrine underwent a major renovation in 1990 and was rededicated on July 8 by H.G. Thomas Mar Athanasios, Metropolitan of the Chengannur Diocese. Following the widening of the adjoining roadway in 2008, the compound wall and entrance gate were reconstructed.

498 families (2022) – Originally established as a filial parish of the Palayam Cathedral, this church is the first in Thiruvananthapuram dedicated to Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios (Parumala Thirumeni). Reverently known as Thekkan Parumala AKA Parumala of the South, it has become one of the principal pilgrimage churches of southern Kerala.

A chapel was established in 1976 after land was acquired in 1972, using materials from the former Sunday School building of the Palayam Cathedral. It was consecrated by H.G. Mathews Mar Coorilos, later H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews II, and was raised to an independent parish in 1985.

Rapid growth led to the expansion of the original chapel in 1988 and the construction of the present church, consecrated on January 12–13, 2001, by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews II. On the same occasion, the Holy Relics of Parumala Thirumeni were solemnly installed, and the church was proclaimed "Thekkan Parumala St. Gregorios Valia Pally."

The parish also established its own cemetery at Malamukal after acquiring 76 cents of land near Nettayam, replacing its earlier reliance on the Palayam Cathedral cemetery. Today, the church remains a major pilgrimage center, drawing devotees from across southern Kerala who seek the intercessions of Parumala Thirumeni regardless of caste or creed.

There are 5 priests (including one late cor-episcopa) from this parish.

ds:
1955 കാലങ്ങളിൽ പള്ളിക്ക് സ്ഥലം കണ്ടെത്തിയപ്പോൾ തന്നെ രാജകുമാരി സൗത്തിൽ ഏകദേശം രണ്ടര ഏക്കർ സ്ഥലം കണ്ടെത്തി അതിൽ ഒരു പള്ളി വയ്ക്കുന്നതിനുവേണ്ടി പ്രാരംഭ നടപടികൾ തുടങ്ങിയിരുന്നു. അതിനായി പോത മുറിച്ചിടുകയും ചെമ്മണ്ണാറിൽ നിന്ന് ഇല്ലി വെട്ടി കൊണ്ടുവരികയും ചെയ്തു. എന്നാൽ വളരെ കുറച്ച് ആളുകൾ മാത്രം ഉള്ളതുകൊണ്ട് രണ്ട് പള്ളി വേണ്ട എന്ന കൂടിയാലോചന പ്രകാരം ഈ പള്ളിയുടെ നടപടിക്രമങ്ങൾ ഉപേക്ഷിച്ച് രാജകുമാരി നോർത്തിൽ ഗലീലാ കുന്നിൽ പള്ളി വയ്ക്കുകയാണ് ഉണ്ടായത്. 1959ൽ കുരുവിള സിറ്റിയിൽ മോർ സ്തേഫാനോസ് സഹദായുടെ നാമധേയത്തിൽ ഒരു കുരിശു സ്ഥാപിക്കുകയും പിന്നീട് മുരുക്കും തൊട്ടി സെന്റ് ജോർജ് യാക്കോബായ സുറിയാനി പള്ളി നിലവിൽ വന്നപ്പോൾ ആ പള്ളിക്ക് ഈ കുരിശടി വിട്ടുകൊടുത്ത് രാജകുമാരി സൗത്തിൽ പണ്ട് പള്ളി വയ്ക്കാനി രുന്ന സ്ഥലത്തിനോട് ചേർന്ന് മോർ സ്തേഫാനോസ് സഹദായുടെയും മോർ ബസേലിയോസ് ബാവ യുടെയും സംയുക്ത നാമത്തിൽ ഒരു കുരിശു സ്ഥാപിക്കുകയും തുടർന്നുള്ള എല്ലാ വർഷങ്ങളിലും ഇടവക പള്ളിയിലെ പെരുന്നാളിനോട് അനുബന്ധിച്ച് പ്രദക്ഷി ണം കടന്നു വരികയും ചെയ്യുന്നു. 1975 ഒക്ടോബർ മാസത്തിൽ രാജകുമാരി സൗത്തിൽ കുരിശിരിക്കുന്ന സ്ഥലത്ത് റോഡിനോട് ചേർന്ന് മോർ സ്തേഫാനോസ് സഹദായുടെയും മോർ ബസേലിയോസ് ബാവയുടെയും സംയുക്ത നാമധേയത്തിൽ കുരിശും തൊട്ടിയുടെ പണികൾ ആരംഭിക്കുകയും 1977 ഫെബ്രുവരി മാസം ആറാം തീയതി പള്ളിയുടെ പെരുന്നാളിനോടനുബന്ധിച്ച് ആബൂൻ മോർ ബസേലിയോസ് പൗലോസ് ദ്വിതിയൻ കാതോലിക്കാബാവയുടെ പ്രധാന കാർമികത്വത്തിലും ഇടവക
മെത്രാപ്പോലീത്ത നി.വ.ദി.ശ്രീ.തോമസ് മാർ ദീവന്നാസിയോസ്, നി വ ദി ശ്രീ ഗീവർഗീസ് മാർ ഗ്രീഗോറിയോസ്, നി. വ. ദി. ശ്രീ കുര്യാക്കോസ് മാർ കൂറീലോസ് എന്നീ മെത്രാപ്പോലീത്തമാരുടെ സഹകാർമികത്വത്തിലും കൂദാശ നിർവഹിക്കുകയുണ്ടായി. പിന്നീട് ശനിയാഴ്ചകളിൽ കുരിശുപള്ളിയിൽ കുർബാന ചൊല്ലുവാൻ ആരംഭിച്ചു.അതേവർഷം സെപ്റ്റംബർ 23 24 തീയതികളിൽ എല്ലാവർഷവും സഹദായുടെയും ബസേലിയോസ് ബാവയുടെയും പെരുന്നാൾ സംയുക്തമായി ആഘോഷപൂർവ്വം കൊണ്ടാടിവരുന്നു
